thread:
arjun: Quick update — I ran a compatibility sweep of FlashAttention v3 vs v2 on staging infra across shapes we care about (chat short, long context, and KV-heavy decoder flows).

mai: Nice. Any headline numbers?

arjun: Short version:
- seq=64, batch=16: v2 ~ 45k tok/s, v3 ~ 41k tok/s (-8%)
- seq=1024, batch=8: v2 ~ 5.2k tok/s, v3 ~ 5.7k tok/s (+9%)
- seq=4096, batch=2: v2 ~ 1.1k tok/s, v3 ~ 1.3k tok/s (+18%)
- KV-heavy (decoder w/ cache warm): tail latency +3-5% on v3 vs v2

samir: interesting—where's the regression coming from? kernel launch overhead? batching?

arjun: Mostly kernel startup and tiled memory copies in v3 for small seq. Profiling trace attached (perf-bot): link: https://internal/perf/trace/1795

lucy: Any KV cache behavior differences? We saw weird eviction thrashing in paged attention earlier.

arjun: v3's paged attention uses a different tile layout so cache hit patterns shift. With our current KV shard/eviction policy we saw ~6% more cache misses at churned session rates (high prefix updates). With a small tweak to prefetch threshold (increase from 128->256 tokens) the misses drop back and latency aligns.

mai: Can you paste the reproduction command + perf flags?

arjun: Sure:
```
# run perf harness
python -m perf.run --model redwood-13b --kernel flashv3 --seq 4096 --batch 2 --kv-mode paged --iters 200
python -m perf.run --model redwood-13b --kernel flashv2 --seq 64 --batch 16 --iters 500
```
Logs are in s3://redwood-perf/staging/1795/

henry: From rollout POV we should gate v3 behind an fflag + kernel-chooser logic. Proposal:
```
if seq_len >= 1024 or (kv_hit_rate > 0.85 and seq_len >= 512): use flashv3_long
elif batch_size <= 16 and seq_len <= 128: use flashv2_short
else: default to flashv2
```
Enable fflag=false by default, canary to internal test teams, then 5% production, monitor token/sec and p99 latency.

samir: Also add a fallback if we observe >5% regression on p95 within 10 minutes: switch to flashv2 for that model+route.

arjun: Agreed. We'll instrument kernel chooser with metrics: chooser.reason, chosen_kernel, perf_delta, kv_hit_rate. Perf-bot will emit alerts on regression.

perf-bot: Automated benchmark job 1795 completed. Summary: flashv3 wins long shapes, loses small-chat shapes. Regression detected for fused-attn+fp16 path in batched shapes: ~4% throughput drop (ticket #4231). :eyes:

lucy: Ticket #4231 assigned to eng-runtime / eng-ml. Might be kernel codegen for fused path.

mai: Plan for next steps?

arjun: 1) Add chooser heuristics + fflag (PR in review). 2) Run targeted AB test with internal canary (5 models). 3) If stable, ramp to 20% traffic with auto-fallback. 4) Investigate fused-attn fp16 regression in parallel.

henry: I'll draft the rollout playbook (inc. runbooks for rollforward/rollback, alert thresholds, and metrics dashboards). Ping me when PR merged.

deploy-bot: Staging gate passed for flashv3-chooser PR #5678. Can start internal canary when ready.

arjun: Thanks — I'll push PR updates today and link the canary list. Will also include a short regression test that runs fused-attn fp16 microbenchmarks on CI.

mai: :thumbsup: keep us posted, esp. on KV prefetch tweak impact.

samir: Adding note: try merging a lightweight batching heuristic too — prefer batching when latency headroom > 20ms.

arjun: Good call. I'll include batching heuristic in PR.

lucy: leaving a short perf checklist in the ticket: measure seq distribution, kv_hit_rate, p50/p95/p99, token/sec, error-counts.

perf-bot: Noted. Creating dashboard: /dashboards/flashv3-chooser-1795

henry: Great thread. Let's execute the staged plan. :rocket:
